# Couchwire 0.2.6: Game volume, and a steadier app
*25 November 2026*
Game sound gets its own volume and mute, you can cancel a connect while the PS5 is waking, and a set of under-the-hood fixes make the app steadier.
### Added
- **Game volume and mute.** A Sound button in the stream controls sets the game's volume on your Mac, separately from the Mac's own volume, and mutes it. **Control-Command-S** mutes and unmutes. The volume is remembered; mute lasts for the session, so the next one never starts silent by surprise. Your microphone isn't affected. - **Cancel while connecting.** The Connecting panel on your home network always has a Cancel button now, and while a console is waking from rest mode its card shows Cancel instead of a spinner.
### Changed
- **Quicker reconnects over the internet.** After a network change, Couchwire keeps asking your PS5 within the same PlayStation Network session instead of starting a new one each time, which saves several seconds. - **Clearer console cards.** The line under a console's name no longer repeats its status. It says what Play will do (wake it, for example) or which network it's on. With your consoles set up, the Nearby section shrinks to a quiet line until a new console turns up. - **One verdict on responsiveness.** The dot in the stream controls and the rating in the performance panel now use the same thresholds, so they never disagree. - **Console Settings shows which console** you're changing, at the top of the sheet. - **Better with VoiceOver.** The settings button on each console card and the close buttons on the stream's banners have proper names, and are easier to click.
### Fixed
- **Sound and haptics never wait.** The parts that play game sound and drive the controller's voice coils no longer wait on a lock, which removes a rare source of crackles. - **Less work per frame.** Each video frame is now copied once on its way to the decoder instead of three times, and the work Couchwire does on each frame before decoding takes about a seventh of the time it did. - **A crash when unplugging the controller.** Couchwire could close the controller's connection while a report from it was still being handled. - **Fewer details in the Mac's log.** Your console's name and network addresses are no longer written to the system log in plain text. - Smaller fixes for pairing and the video decoder that could leave a little memory behind or, rarely, misbehave.
**Update:** Couchwire 0.1.0 and later offer this update by themselves; or choose **Couchwire › Check for Updates…**. New here? Download `Couchwire-0.2.6.dmg`, open it, and drag Couchwire onto Applications. Needs macOS 14 or later on Apple silicon. The app is not notarised, so the first time macOS may say it cannot verify it: open System Settings > Privacy & Security, scroll to the message about Couchwire and click **Open Anyway**.
**Source:** Couchwire is free software under the GNU AGPL v3. `Couchwire-0.2.6-source.tar.gz` is the source of this release, including chiaki-ng, and `Couchwire-0.2.6-dependencies-source.tar` holds the exact sources of the libraries it's built with.

# Couchwire 0.2.5: A sharper picture after Wi-Fi hiccups
*24 November 2026*
At home, a short Wi-Fi stall no longer leaves the picture soft for the rest of the session, and if the picture does go soft after a longer bad patch, Couchwire offers to sharpen it again.
### Added
- **A sharp picture through short Wi-Fi stalls.** When it hears about lost video, your PS5 lowers the picture quality hard and then takes up to half an hour to raise it again. A few seconds of trouble, such as macOS scanning for Wi-Fi networks when you open the Wi-Fi menu, could leave the picture soft for a long time. At home, Couchwire now keeps short stalls to itself. If the trouble lasts, it tells the PS5 as before, so the PS5 can still ease off when the network is really busy. - **Sharpen.** If the picture is still soft after the connection has recovered, a banner offers to restart the stream. A fresh stream starts at full quality, and the restart takes a few seconds. At home only. - **An AirDrop tip.** On Wi-Fi, when AirDrop is on, the struggling banner says that turning AirDrop off in Control Centre can help. AirDrop makes the Mac's Wi-Fi leave your network for moments at a time.
**Update:** Couchwire 0.1.0 and later offer this update by themselves; or choose **Couchwire › Check for Updates…**. New here? Download `Couchwire-0.2.5.dmg`, open it, and drag Couchwire onto Applications. Needs macOS 14 or later on Apple silicon. The app is not notarised, so the first time macOS may say it cannot verify it: open System Settings > Privacy & Security, scroll to the message about Couchwire and click **Open Anyway**.

# Couchwire 0.2.4: Rumble that feels right, and quicker reconnects
*23 November 2026*
Vibration and trigger effects follow your PS5 more closely, full DualSense haptics start when you plug in a cable mid-game, and Couchwire gets back to your game faster after a network change.
### Changed
- **Vibration follows your PS5's settings.** Couchwire now uses the PS5's Vibration Intensity and Trigger Effect Intensity settings. Weak and Medium soften the rumble and the triggers, and Off turns them off. - **Gentler rumble over Bluetooth.** Over Bluetooth the controller can't play the PS5's haptics directly, so Couchwire turns them into rumble. That rumble is now less heavy-handed, ignores very faint signals and never falls behind the game. - **Quicker reconnects.** After a network change, or when you close a stream and press Play again, the PS5 takes a few seconds to let go of the old stream. Couchwire now asks again every second while it waits, and says it's waiting, instead of showing "already in use". Back on your home network it reconnects as soon as it finds the PS5. - **The struggling banner goes away** once the stream recovers, and comes back only if it gets bad again.
### Fixed
- **Full haptics over USB mid-game.** Plugging the controller in with a cable during a stream now switches to the DualSense's full haptics within a second or two. Before, it stayed on Bluetooth-style rumble until the next stream. - **Trigger effects no longer restart by themselves.** Couchwire re-sent them every second, which could restart a vibrating trigger effect or click a weapon trigger again. - **Moving from home Wi-Fi to a hotspot** goes over the internet straight away, instead of trying the home address again first. - **A reconnect no longer lowers your quality.** The first 30 seconds after a network change, while the Wi-Fi settles, no longer count towards automatic quality or bring up the struggling banner.

Download `Couchwire-0.2.4.dmg`, open it, and drag Couchwire onto Applications. Needs macOS 14 or later on Apple silicon. The app is not notarised, so the first time macOS may say it cannot verify it: open System Settings > Privacy & Security, scroll to the message about Couchwire and click **Open Anyway**.
